blocks.purpose: One or two lines of plain words with numbers filled in from live data. The headline of a goal is usually a sentence.
How far a value has got along a scale, with marks on the scale and a lighter extension for where it is heading.
One metric over time as a line, bars or dots, with optional reference lines, a shaded band, and a dashed line showing where the current rate leads.
Which days something happened: one ring per day for a week, or a calendar of cells for several weeks.
Either the goal's own one-off steps, or a ladder of thresholds a value climbs.
Dated marks on a line from today: a deadline, a projected finish.
A quick way for the person to record one number for a metric they log by hand.
A few plain words that no data can supply.
A web page the person can open, for data the engine cannot chart.

functions.result: How many days have a value above zero, over the window or all of it.
Whole days until the end of the current week or month (period), or until a date (date). Give exactly one.
args[0] divided by args[1]; unknown when args[1] is zero.
How much of the current week or month has passed, from 0 to 1.
The date the metric reaches args[0] at its current rate; unknown when it is not heading there.
The oldest value of the metric.
The newest value of the metric.
The largest of two to four calculations.
The average of the metric's values, over the window or all of it.
The smallest of two to four calculations.
Where the metric's running total for the period is heading, at its pace so far.
How fast the metric changes, per day, week or month, from its first to its latest value.
Consecutive days up to today with a value above zero.
The values of the metric added up, over the window or all of it.

catalogs.limits: 1-8 blocks; 0-6 metrics; a calculation nests five levels; a sentence has at most six slots.

guidance: Compose this goal's view from the kit, as a designer would for this one goal: lead with what the person most wants to know, in a sentence with live numbers; draw it the way its shape suggests; leave out whatever does not help. A metric is a data source: a provider series (source), a routine's logs (routine_id), or numbers the person logs (neither). The app does all arithmetic from live data, so never write a figure yourself: bind to a metric and use a function. If nothing in the kit fits, use text.
